title: Atlas Vault Traversal
subtitle: Escape the document library and then seal it
summary: Atlas Logistics serves partner documents through a download endpoint that trusts the requested file name. Walk out of the public folder to reach an internal document, then apply the containment policy and verify it.
scenario: Atlas Logistics publishes partner paperwork through a small Node service. The endpoint was written quickly: it joins user input onto a public directory and normalises the result. Your job is to demonstrate the traversal, capture the internal marker, and then block the class of attack.
learningObjectives: Exploit path traversal in a real download handler
Explain how normalisation after concatenation enables escape
Apply a containment check and verify it blocks payloads without breaking downloads
authorizedScope: Only the Atlas Logistics training service inside this session. All documents are synthetic.
riskSummary: Path traversal lets an attacker read files outside an intended directory, including configuration, credentials and internal documents.
remediation: Resolve the requested file against an allowed base directory, reject traversal segments early, canonicalise, then verify the final path still starts with the base directory before reading.
conclusion: You escaped a public directory using a normalised relative path, captured the internal marker, and then blocked the attack at the edge while keeping legitimate downloads working.

objectives.title: Read the internal document
objectives.description: The public library only lists three files, but the service resolves paths relative to a public directory. Read an internal document and submit the marker it contains.
objectives.evidencePrompt: Submit the CF{...} marker from the internal document.

hints.text: The handler builds `public/<file>` and normalises the result. Try `file=../internal/flag.txt` (URL-encode the dots if your shell mangles them).

objectives.title: Block traversal at the service
objectives.description: Enable the containment policy through the authenticated admin API. The live check sends a traversal payload and confirms it is rejected while a normal download still works.

hints.text: Apply `{"blockTraversal": true}` with `labctl policy apply` and re-test both requests.

walkthrough.title: Download a normal document
walkthrough.body: Confirm the endpoint works with a legitimate file name.

walkthrough.title: Traverse out of the public directory
walkthrough.body: The handler normalises `public/../internal/flag.txt` to `internal/flag.txt`. Read it.

walkthrough.title: Block the attack
walkthrough.body: Apply the policy, then re-run the traversal: it should return invalid_path while normal downloads continue.
